IMPLEMENTATION COMPLETE. `analysis.py` implements a process-based fixed-3-layer snowpack model (hourly forcing, 60-s substeps) and all four required artifacts are written and validated: `analysis.py`, `results/snow_state.npy` (float64, exactly (68,3,5), last axis [thickness_m, density_kg_m3, ice_mm, liq_mm, temp_K]), `results/snow_summary.csv` (68 rows; columns day,swe_mm,snow_depth_m,melt_mm,refreeze_mm,runoff_mm,mean_density_kg_m3; day=1..68), and `results/snow_evolution.png` (4-panel diagnostic: SWE/depth, layer temperatures, layer densities, daily melt/refreeze/runoff). matplotlib is unavailable in this runtime (no network, PIL extensions are cp314-only), so the figure was produced by a self-contained pure-stdlib PNG renderer built into analysis.py; the matplotlib path is retained and used automatically where matplotlib exists.

MODEL (as approved): surface energy balance at a zero-heat-capacity skin (absorbed SW at ALBEDO=0.80, net LW with eps=0.98, bulk sensible/latent with WIND_SPEED=2 m/s, C_H=C_E=2e-3, RH=75% — all explicit named constants; skin pinned at 273.15 K with surplus energy converted to surface melt); inter-layer + ground thermal diffusion (Sturm et al. 1997 k_eff, harmonic-mean interface values, fixed basal T_GROUND=272.15 K with K_GROUND=0.4 W/m/K); cold-content-limited melt and instantaneous refreeze of held liquid (latent heat warms the layer); ice and liquid as separate state variables in every layer; top-down percolation with irreducible holding capacity THETA_IRR=0.04 of pore volume, bottom excess = runoff; SNTHERM/Anderson-style overburden compaction via a viscosity increasing with density (+1.5 e-folds/50 kg/m3) and decreasing with temperature and liquid content, density capped at 917 kg/m3; snowfall added to the top layer at FRESH_SNOW_RHO=120 kg/m3 and T=min(T_air,273.15 K); thickness/density recomputed from conserved mass after every update (density=(ice+liq)/thickness holds by construction).

REQUESTED DIAGNOSTICS: (1) MASS CLOSURE: per-day residual max = 1.7e-12 mm (machine precision); 68-day cumulative: snowfall 67.8384 + rainfall 0 + deposition 4.5002 - sublimation 8.7947 - runoff 24.4945 - evaporation 0 = +39.0494 mm = dSWE (209.797 -> 248.847 mm), exact to <1e-11. (2) BOTTOM-LAYER TEMPERATURE trajectory: min 272.088 K, max 273.150 K, mean 272.623 K over the 68 daily snapshots — stays within [T_ground-1K, 273.15 K] at all times (True); it sits slightly above the 272.15 K boundary late in the run because refrozen meltwater warms the base, and dips 0.06 K below it only through transient conduction with the colder mid layer. (3) STEP-INSENSITIVITY: dt=60 s vs 600 s gives identical evolution (final SWE 248.847 vs 248.840 mm, 3e-5 relative; melt 140.15 vs 140.15; all other diagnostics unchanged) — the substep scheme is stable and step-insensitive. (4) Additional energy-consistency diagnostic (enthalpy relative to liquid water at 273.15 K vs. integrated surface+ground fluxes, precipitation/sublimation/runoff enthalpy): relative error 8.4e-4 in production and <=1.2e-3 in every sensitivity run.

KEY RESULTS (production run): SWE 209.8 -> 248.8 mm (mean 236.1, max 250.7); depth 1.340 -> 1.721 m; bulk density 156.6 -> 144.6 kg/m3 (min 144.6, max 163.8); daily melt mean 2.06 mm (max 3.70), refreeze mean 0.82 (max 1.57), runoff first appears ~day 45 (mean 0.36, max 2.50); season totals: melt 140.15 mm (gross), refreeze 55.40 mm, runoff 24.49 mm, sublimation 8.79 mm, rime deposition 4.50 mm. Physics narrative: clear-sky radiative cooling is largely offset by assumed turbulent heat supply, so the pack ripens quickly (top layer liquid at 0 C from ~day 8), then runs a diurnal melt-refreeze cycle; meltwater infiltrates and refreezes in the mid and bottom layers (their ice grows 73.4 -> 74.2 and 98.7 mm), runoff starts only once the deeper holding capacity fills; compaction counteracts ~0.57 m of added snowfall depth. Bottom line: the snowpack survives the season with net +39 mm SWE.

SENSITIVITY NOTE (turbulent fluxes govern late-season melt, as flagged): radiation-only (C_H=C_E=0) gives gross melt 174.3 mm (+24%) and runoff 28.7 mm but similar final SWE 247.2 mm (nighttime refreeze rises to 81.2 mm, compensating); doubling turbulent transfer (C_H=4e-3) gives melt 120.3 mm (-14%), runoff 17.0 mm, SWE 244.7 mm (stronger sublimation 17.1 mm). Albedo dominates: alpha=0.90 -> almost no melt (7.8 mm, SWE 279.7); alpha=0.70 -> gross melt 164.0 mm and upper-layer ablation with 31.2 mm of ponded-water evaporation (SWE 214.2, a degenerate regime handled by the documented evaporation sink). K_GROUND 0.1 W/m/K leaves melt unchanged (140.15, melt is skin-driven) but reduces basal refreeze (36.7 vs 55.4) and increases runoff to 42.3 mm. All variants close mass to <=4e-13 mm/day and energy to <=1.2e-3.

LIMITATIONS: turbulent parameters, albedo, fresh-snow density (120 kg/m3), THETA_IRR, ground boundary (272.15 K, k=0.4), and compaction viscosities are assumed, not measured (forcing file contains no wind/RH/soil data); results are conditional on them as quantified above. The forcing is synthetic (constant daily 600 W/m2 clear-sky peak, constant pressure); day numbering in the CSV is 1-based (day 1 = first 24 h). No rainfall occurs in this forcing, but rain-on-snow is implemented. Precipitation phase needed no partitioning model: rainfall is identically zero and all 36 snowfall hours have T_air<0 C (verified at inspection).
